mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate relative to its recent 12-month average signals an accommodative monetary policy shift, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return distribution in periods with FEDFUNDS below 1.0% shows no statistically significant positive mean compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate exceeds 4.5%, it indicates labor market weakness that suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where UNRATE > 4.5%, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) falls below 0.5% and monthly housing starts (HOUST) drop below 1200.0 units, it indicates a weakening demand environment that reduces corporate profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where GDPC1 growth rate < 0.5% and HOUST < 1200.0, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When CPIAUCSL exceeds 240.0, it signals persistent inflation that triggers aggressive monetary tightening, increasing risk-free rates and reducing equity multiples, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 240.0, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (INDPRO) indicates robust manufacturing activity that supports corporate earnings growth, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward return distribution in periods with INDPRO growth shows no statistically significant positive mean compared to the baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1200.0 units, it reflects a contraction in the residential construction sector that reduces consumer confidence and spending, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In instances where HOUST < 1200.0, the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of cases, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in labor force participation (PAYEMS) and the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicate a weakening labor market coupled with monetary easing, which reduces corporate profit margins and stock valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: labor market weakness with monetary easing
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where PAYEMS growth rate < 0% and FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: In recessionary conditions (UNRATE > 4.5%), the labor market deterioration suppresses consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances where UNRATE > 4.5%, or the mean return is not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.05).
